narrative:
Your loan application was denied because our assessment estimated a 41% likelihood of credit risk, which exceeds our approval threshold of 25%.

The most influential factor working against you was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, over 70% had no checking account at all, and very few carried a negative balance. This raised the most significant concern for the assessment.

On a more positive note, your credit history actually worked in your favor. Having critical or other existing credits is common among approved applicants — roughly 41% of those approved share a similar credit history — and this factor pushed the assessment toward a more favorable view of your application.

Similarly, the purpose of your loan — purchasing a used car — also contributed positively to your profile, as this is a recognized and relatively common reason for borrowing among approved applicants.

However, other aspects of your profile added pressure beyond the top three factors. You are currently unemployed, which is extremely rare among approved applicants (less than 2%). You are also requesting 6,615 DM, more than double the average loan amount of 2,845 DM among approved applicants, over a 24-month period compared to an average of 18 months. Your installment repayments would consume 25–35% of your disposable income, and you have no property listed as security.

We recommend addressing your employment situation first, as securing stable income would significantly strengthen a future application. Reducing the requested loan amount and improving your checking account balance would also help considerably.

prompt:
A machine learning model predicted that a loan applicant represents a BAD CREDIT RISK and therefore their loan application was DENIED. Your goal is to generate an explanatory narrative based on the information provided (1-5), explaining why the loan application was denied for this applicant.

1. DATASET INFORMATION
The dataset contains information on a series of debtors that took a loan from the bank.

The target variable is whether the applicant will be a bad credit risk.

Protected attributes sex, age and foreign_worker were not used to make the machine prediction.

2. TECHNICAL EXPLANATION: SHAP VALUES
A SHAP value tells you how much a feature influenced the prediction (larger absolute value means a stronger influence) and its direction: positive pushes toward bad credit risk, negative toward good credit risk. Below are the top 3 features by absolute SHAP value.

3. APPLICANT PROFILE
You are writing a narrative tailored to this specific applicant, who was denied a loan.
Feature values (with comparisons to approved applicants where available, showing the distribution or average among approved applicants):
- status = <0 DM (status of checking account) - distribution: none: 71.2%, <0 DM: 13.6%, ≥200 DM/salary: 7.6%, 0-200 DM: 7.6%
- duration = 24 (duration of credit request in months) - average: 18.2
- credit_history = critical/other credits (credit history rating) - distribution: existing paid: 51.5%, critical/other credits: 40.9%, past delays: 6.1%, no credits/all paid: 1.5%
- purpose = used car (purpose of credit) - distribution: radio/TV: 37.9%, furniture/equipment: 22.7%, new car: 13.6%, used car: 13.6%, business: 7.6%, education: 3.0%, repairs: 1.5%
- amount = 6615 (amount of credit requested in DM) - average: 2845.2
- savings = <100 DM (savings account status) - distribution: <100 DM: 45.5%, unknown/none: 33.3%, 100-500 DM: 12.1%, 500-1000 DM: 6.1%, ≥1000 DM: 3.0%
- employment_duration = unemployed (employment duration) - distribution: 1-4 years: 34.8%, ≥7 years: 34.8%, 4-7 years: 21.2%, <1 year: 7.6%, unemployed: 1.5%
- installment_rate = 25-35% (installment rate as percentage of disposable income) - distribution: <20%: 51.5%, 25-35%: 22.7%, 20-25%: 15.2%, ≥35%: 10.6%
- sex = male (the sex of the applicant)
- other_debtors = none (other debtors/guarantors) - distribution: none: 87.9%, co-applicant: 6.1%, guarantor: 6.1%
- present_residence = 4 (years at present residence) - average: 2.9
- property = unknown/none (property status) - distribution: car/other: 37.9%, real estate: 37.9%, building society/life insurance: 19.7%, unknown/none: 4.5%
- age = 25 (the age of the applicant in years)
- other_installment_plans = none (other installment plans) - distribution: none: 95.5%, stores: 3.0%, bank: 1.5%
- housing = for free (housing situation) - distribution: own: 80.3%, rent: 16.7%, for free: 3.0%
- number_credits = 2 (number of existing credits at this bank) - average: 1.4
- job = management/self-employed/highly skilled (job type) - distribution: skilled/official: 65.2%, unskilled-resident: 21.2%, management/self-employed/highly skilled: 12.1%, unemployed/unskilled-non-resident: 1.5%
- people_liable = 1 (number of people financially dependent) - average: 1.2
- telephone = yes registered (has a telephone or not) - distribution: none: 57.6%, yes registered: 42.4%
- foreign_worker = yes (foreign worker or not)


The model's prediction:
- Predicted probability of bad credit risk: 41.0%
- Decision threshold: a predicted probability of bad credit risk of 25% or higher leads to this decision.

4. FEATURE IMPORTANCE ANALYSIS (Ranked by Influence)
       Feature  SHAP_Value
        status    0.083835
credit_history   -0.076371
       purpose   -0.040337

5. YOUR NARRATIVE TASK
Write a detailed narrative explanation tailored to this non-technical reader that MUST explain:
1) The model's predicted probability of bad credit risk and what this means for the applicant.
2) Why the loan application was denied: which features were most important in driving this prediction and why (focus on the ranking of most important features).
3) How each of the top 3 most important features contributed (either pushing toward bad credit risk or toward good credit risk).
4) What the applicant should do next.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Do not use the numeric SHAP values in your answer. Instead, discuss the ranking and direction of influence.
- Do not talk about model internals, algorithms, or training details.
- Do not include greeting or closing statements, nor bullet points or tables.
STYLE:
- Length: 250 words maximum.
- Write a coherent narrative directly addressing the applicant.
- Do NOT copy-paste feature names, but instead incorporate them naturally in the narrative.
- Include feature values and their comparisons to averages or distributions, but reserve this for features where it really clarifies the explanation.
